newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Supreme Court allows seizure of Marcos land.
newsitem.headline: Manila Supreme Court allows seizure of Marcos land.

text.p: The Philippine Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a petition by the son of late dictator Ferdinand Marcos to stop the seizure of land because of failure to pay tax.
Ferdinand Marcos II asked the Supreme Court to annul a lower court decision to sell 11 plots of land in central Leyte province to cover 23.4 billion pesos ($887 million) in unpaid land taxes.
Marcos argued the tax demands were full of innacuracies.
However, the Court said neither the former president nor his heirs had ever questioned the 1991 assessment.
"In view of all the foregoing, we rule that the deficiency income tax assessments and estate tax assessment, are already final and unappealable," the Court said in its 20-page decision.
Marcos ruled the Philippines for 20 years with an iron fist, amassing a fortune in the process.
He was overthrown and forced into exile in 1986 and the Philippine government subsequently sequestered all suspected ill-gotten wealth of his family and associates.
